To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the interferon system is a major component of the cellular immune response to HIV infection, 2) IFN-alpha/beta are the most important IFN for the cellular immune response, 3) the cellular immune response is a key determinant of the clinical manifestations of HIV infection, 4) the cellular immune system is the major determinant for the development of AIDS, and 5) the cellular immune reactivity is a major determinant for the efficacy of anti-retroviral therapies.

(1) HIV infection of cells of the immune system leads to a decrease in the production of IFN-γ and IFN-α/β by these cells; and (2) the decrease in production of IFN is associated with a decrease in the number of IFN receptors on the cell surface and is not due to a decrease in IFN receptor affinity.
IFN-gamma and IFN-beta, but not IFN-alpha, inhibit HIV-1 replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biology of the IFN, and the role of IFN in host resistance to HIV infection.
understanding the molecular biology of IFNs, the mechanisms of their action in cells, and their interactions in vivo with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
the role of IFNs in the immune response to HIV infection, and the effect of HIV infection on the expression of the IFN genes and on the cellular response to the IFNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interferons, in addition to their well-known antiviral effects, have a wide variety of immunologic effects.
interferons are not only important to our understanding of the biology of HIV infection but also to the development of new therapeutic modalities.
IFN is an important component of host defense, and that it is involved in a number of cellular and molecular events in HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFN-γ is a major component of HIV pathogenesis, whereas IFN-α and IFN-β are important in the control and treatment of HIV infection.
IFN is the most potent immunoregulatory molecule known to date, and that the IFN system has a central role in the pathogenesis of HIV infection.
IFN-α and β are the most effective antiretroviral agents known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFNs are important for the control of HIV-1 replication, both by direct effects on viral replication and by indirect effects on the host immune system.
IFN-alpha and IFN-beta are the most effective antiviral molecules in the treatment of HIV disease.
IFN-alpha is a potent inhibitor of HIV-1 replication, which may have therapeutic implications in the treatment of AIDS patients.
